diagnoses.analysis: The Jedis 2.3 callback pipeline returns a new generic JedisDataException whose cause is the protocol-confirmed server exception. Identity checking only the wrapper loses the WRONGTYPE classification. The Jedis 2 getter now checks the confirmed immediate cause of an unconfirmed generic wrapper, preserving dedicated/client exception fallback and the actual recorded exception. The callback agent regression passes in default and preview semconv modes on Java 25 and Java 8.

This Java 25 deny-unsafe check has the same Jedis 2.3 callback wrapper-identity failure, repeated by the test retry mechanism. Recognizing its protocol-confirmed immediate cause fixes the classification without changing unsafe access or exception propagation. Focused unit and installed-agent checks pass on Java 25 and Java 8; the deny-unsafe matrix itself was not rerun locally.

The Java 11 failure is the same returned Jedis 2.3 wrapper losing protocol-error identity. The getter fix recognizes only a confirmed immediate cause of a generic JedisDataException. Its focused callback regression and fallback unit coverage pass on Java 25 and Java 8; Java 11 was not rerun locally.

The Java 25 check repeatedly fails the callback pipeline assertion because Response.get wraps the confirmed protocol error. The getter now resolves that confirmed immediate cause for error.type, while the wrapper remains the recorded exception. The complete Jedis 2 unit suite and callback agent regression in both semconv modes pass on Java 25 and Java 8.

The Java 8 check has the same Jedis 2.3 generic-wrapper identity mismatch. The focused callback regression now verifies WRONGTYPE on spans and duration metrics and no error.type on a subsequent successful command. Both semconv variants and the full Jedis 2 unit suite pass locally on Java 8 and Java 25.

The Java 27 failure is the same version-specific Jedis 2.3 response wrapper, not a Java 27-specific API or runtime issue. The confirmed-cause getter fix and callback/fallback regressions pass on Java 25 and Java 8. Java 27 was not rerun locally.

The Java 21 failure is the same callback pipeline wrapping a protocol-confirmed server exception. The Jedis 2 getter now classifies the confirmed immediate cause only for generic JedisDataException wrappers. Focused installed-agent and fallback unit tests pass on Java 25 and Java 8; Java 21 was not rerun locally.

The PR changed ExecAdvice.stopSpan to accept the returned List before TransactionState, but its empty-transaction unit caller still passes two arguments. The caller now supplies a null result. compileUnitTestsJava and all 59 Jedis 2 unit tests pass on Java 25 and Java 8.

The latest-dependency job includes the same fixed Jedis 2.3 callback wrapper-classification failure. It also has an unrelated pre-existing topology-test failure: a CLUSTER slots request ends with Unexpected end of stream, then a successful retry produces a second CLUSTER span while the test expects exactly one. The aggregate-target test and cluster connection-acquisition instrumentation are unchanged between the frozen merge base and head; the PR adds error classification but no topology retry or connection behavior. No unrelated topology code or assertion was changed. The new callback regression uses the same fixed Jedis 2.3 suite dependency and passes in both semconv modes on Java 25 and Java 8; the complete latest-dependency job was not rerun locally.

Classify Redis server errors for Jedis 2, 3, and 4+ on spans and database duration metrics. A confirmed `WRONGTYPE details` reply produces `error.type="WRONGTYPE"`.

Preserve usable ASCII prefixes verbatim. Dedicated server exceptions, non-ASCII or missing prefixes, and client failures retain exception-class fallback. Successful operations omit `error.type`.

Propagate actual failures through command, pipeline, and transaction completion, including error results returned inside batches.
